observation_summary: Numeric character references with values exceeding 0xFFFF are incorrectly converted to arbitrary characters instead of being preserved as literal strings.
reasoning_summary: The code fails to correctly handle numeric character references that exceed the maximum value of a Java char (0xFFFF). When the unescape logic encounters a numeric entity like '&#12345678;', it attempts to parse the number and cast it to a character. Because 12345678 is significantly larger than 65535, the cast results in an incorrect character representation (truncation), whereas the specification requires that invalid or out-of-range numeric entities should be treated as literal text rather than being converted to an incorrect character.
